- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 1–2% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 5-day avg > 80.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements; apply 1.5–3% upward bias to final 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3 or above), model lags; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead and add 0.5–1.0% to final 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate true volatility; increase forecast standard deviation by 10–20% for next 5 days.
